passages.section: Common Tasks and Navigation Guide from Chapter Leader Portal > Task: Report Chapter Events
passages.text:
Typical Process
Chapter Websites Hosted on Engage
Current and accurate chapter websites are a key component to communicating benefits, programs, events, and other important information to current and prospective members.
ISACA offers free website hosting to all chapters as microsites of the global Engage portal. Chapters are not required to use the Engage chapter website, but it offers myriad tools and services to help communicate your chapter’s great work. ISACA Global strongly recommends chapters take advantage of this free tool.
Note: Chapters that choose not to utilize their Engage website still must enter their events into Event Manager on Engage for chapter compliance.
Benefits of Engage-hosted chapter websites include:
Email Communication Tool – Allows you to easily disseminate information to your chapter members via email from the chapter website.

passages.section: Common Tasks and Navigation Guide from Chapter Leader Portal > Task: Report Chapter Events
passages.text:
Event Manager – This Engage event registration tool and calendar allows you to create and manage a variety of event types for your chapter, from online webinars to large, multi-day conferences with numerous registration options and sessions. Adding chapter events into Event Manager will also display them on the Global Events Calendar on Engage, with tags to help publicize your chapter’s event to a broader audience and categorize events by region.
Chapter Library – Use this central location to upload presentations, documents, articles, or other important information relevant to chapter members. All members of your chapter have access.
Member Directory – Connect and network with other IT professionals from your chapter. (Privacy settings enable searchability once a user has logged into Engage and can be managed from their Engage profile at any time.)

passages.section: Common Tasks and Navigation Guide from Chapter Leader Portal > Task: Report Chapter Events
passages.text:
Cross-site Configuration – ISACA Global, Engage, and your chapter website are all linked (i.e., “talk to each other”), which allows for a personalized experience when you log into Engage/your chapter website and cross publication of chapter events.
Job Board Code– Chapters will receive a unique code to share with local employers to post on ISACA’s Job Board for free. The job board postings are managed by ISACA’s Career Center vendor, taking the administrative burden off chapters to edit, manage, or expire old posts on their website.
Globally Managed Assets – The administrative burden is reduced by having ISACA Global services and initiatives automatically displayed on certain chapter website pages.
Community Slideshow – Chapters can easily display photos from chapter events and programs to showcase the member experience and your chapter’s services.

passages.section: Common Tasks and Navigation Guide from Chapter Leader Portal > Task: Report Chapter Events
passages.text:
Upgraded Site Design – The modern, streamlined design and navigation aligns with the ISACA Global Brand. Iconography is available to further assist with design.
Exclusive member-only pages – Create member-only content on your chapter website.

passages.section: Task: Access Compliance Information > Typical Process
passages.text:
Compliance
Annual Chapter Compliance Reporting: 1 November and 31 December.
Each year, chapters confirm that they meet 11 governance, financial, and operational requirements. The compliance process helps protect your chapter, supports strong governance, and maintains your chapter's affiliation with ISACA.
Submit your chapter's compliance report between 1 November and 31 December.
Compliance LIVE Webinar
Join the Compliance LIVE Webinar on 13 October at 10:00 am CT for key updates, practical tips, and answers to common questions.
Register Now
Compliance Support Sessions
Join a monthly Compliance Support Session for live Q&A and guidance on your compliance application, documentation, evidence, and OpenWater submission.
Fill out form to Register: 2026 Compliance Support Sessions
How to Complete Your Submission
Review the compliance rubric and all 11 requirements.

passages.section: Task: Access Compliance Information > Typical Process
passages.text:
Confirm whether your chapter meets each requirement.
Gather supporting documentation using the rubrics evidence examples.
Contact ISACA before the deadline if you need assistance.
Submit your Compliance Documentation
Compliance Requirements
The Compliance Rubric explains each requirement and includes examples of acceptable supporting documentation. Use it as your primary reference when completing the annual compliance review.
Access the 2026 Compliance Rubric
Reduce Year-End Work
Successful compliance begins long before the application is due. Boards should plan early, maintain records throughout the year, monitor progress regularly, and submit using organized, current evidence.
Suggested Timeline
Q1: Governance Documentation 
Plan early by confirming responsibilities and maintaining governance records.
Q2: Bylaws and Privacy Review 
Review key policies and update documentation as needed.

passages.section: Task: Access Compliance Information > Typical Process
passages.text:
Q3: Event Reporting and Audit Preparation 
Maintain event and financial records to support the year-end financial audit.
Q4: Audit Completion and Compliance Submission 
Finalize the audit and submit your compliance application.
Frequently Misunderstood Requirements
Bylaws Review 
Submitting bylaws alone does not demonstrate compliance. Chapters should document that the board reviewed the bylaws during the year in their meeting minutes, which should be available to ISACA Global for review if requested.
Financial Reporting 
Submit the most recent qualifying financial review, audit, approved compilation (with full written approval from ISACA Global for the current year), or verification document. Local legal requirements take precedence when they are more restrictive. More information and link to template are on the rubric.
Educational Events

passages.section: Task: Access Compliance Information > Typical Process
passages.text:
Chapters must conduct at least four educational events and post them on Engage and/or your chapter website. Past events may be added if needed. Please share links in the submission form to indicate where this information can be found.
Privacy Policy 
Review your privacy policy periodically to ensure it remains accurate and aligned with local requirements.
Need Help?
Contact ISACA Support before the Compliance deadline if:
You may not meet a compliance requirement.
You are unsure what compliance evidence is acceptable.
Local laws affect compliance.
You need to discuss available options.
Early communication creates the best opportunity to resolve issues and provide clarity.

This document provides an overview of the primary systems and tools used by ISACA chapter leaders. It is intended to help users understand where information and activities are managed across ISACA's chapter ecosystem. It does not include access-controlled information, member data, or direct system access instructions.

The Chapter Leader Portal serves as the primary operational resource center for ISACA chapter leaders. It provides access to chapter management tools, compliance resources, reports, forms, guidance, and chapter administration functions. Chapter leaders use the portal to support the governance and operation of their chapter.

- Access chapter compliance resources
- Review chapter reporting requirements
- Access chapter management tools
- Submit or support chapter administrative processes
- Access chapter forms and guidance
- Verify chapter membership status when authorized
- Access chapter-related reports and operational resources

C360 (Chapter 360) is ISACA's chapter enablement and management framework designed to support volunteer chapter leaders in operating effective, sustainable chapters. It helps leaders understand chapter operations, governance practices, and organizational maturity across key areas of chapter management.

- View chapter operational information
- Monitor chapter health and performance indicators
- Support governance and planning activities
- Review chapter maturity and operational practices
- Support leadership decision-making
- Access chapter-related metrics and organizational information

Engage is ISACA's online community and collaboration platform. It enables chapter leaders, volunteers, and members to connect, communicate, share knowledge, manage chapter websites, and support chapter activities.

- Participate in chapter leader communities
- Collaborate with other chapter leaders worldwide
- Access community discussions and resources
- Manage ISACA-hosted chapter websites
- Manage chapter events through Event Manager
- Access training materials and support resources
ISACA chapters use several reporting and submission tools to support operational and compliance requirements.

passages.section: Chapter Reporting Tools > Chapter Compliance Reporting
passages.text: Used to submit annual chapter compliance information and demonstrate adherence to the requirements of the Chapter Affiliation Agreement. Compliance reports are submitted annually through designated reporting systems.
Used to record chapter educational events and maintain chapter activity records. Event reporting supports chapter compliance requirements and member engagement tracking.

passages.section: Chapter Reporting Tools > CPE Upload Tool
passages.text: Allows chapter leaders to upload continuing professional education (CPE) attendance information for chapter event participants. This helps members receive appropriate educational credit for participation in chapter events.

passages.section: Chapter Reporting Tools > Board and Leader Roster Management
passages.text: Supports the maintenance and updating of chapter leadership records and authorized chapter contacts.

Chapter Leader Portal
- Operational hub for chapter leaders
- Access point for tools, forms, reports, and governance resources
C360
- Chapter management, performance, and enablement information
- Supports chapter oversight and planning
Engage
- Community, collaboration, websites, and event management
- Supports communication and member engagement
Reporting Tools
- Event reporting
- CPE reporting
- Administrative submissions
Together, these systems support chapter governance, operations, compliance, leadership collaboration, member engagement, and reporting activities across the ISACA chapter ecosystem.

Welcome!
Congratulations, and welcome to your role as the chapter president of your ISACA chapter!
The chapter president serves as the chief elected officer of the chapter and the
primary local representative of ISACA. As the leader of the chapter’s board and
volunteer organization, the president provides strategic direction, fosters effective
governance, and supports the achievement of the chapter’s mission and objectives.
Working collaboratively with the board, volunteers, and staff (where applicable), the
President helps ensure that chapter’s programs, services, and operations deliver value
to members, promote professional growth and engagement and contribute to the
chapter’s long-term sustainability and success.
The Chapter President is responsible for implementing the policies and decisions of the
chapter board by:

• Ensuring the chapter operates in accordance with its bylaws, board-approved policies, and
applicable ISACA Global requirements, and
• Exercising appropriate leadership and judgment to address operational matters
when specific policies or procedures have not been established, while remaining
accountable to the chapter board.
Additionally, the Chapter President should:
• Lead the chapter’s annual strategic planning process, working with the chapter
board to establish goals and objectives that support member value, chapter
sustainability, and alignment with ISACA’s global mission and strategic
priorities.
• Monitor chapter performance and compliance with applicable ISACA Global and
chapter requirements. If the chapter experiences challenges meeting established
standards, the President should promptly engage the Chapter Experience team
through ISACA Support for guidance and assistance.

• Provide leadership and oversight to the chapter board and volunteer leadership
structure, ensuring effective coordination among officers, directors, committee
chairs, and other volunteers in support of the chapter’s strategic goals.
Foster collaboration, accountability, and succession planning within the chapter’s
leadership team to promote continuity and long-term success.
Roles and Responsibilities of the Chapter
President
Regional Strategic Advisory Council
All chapter presidents are ex-officio members of ISACA’s Regional Strategic Advisory
Council (SAC). The SAC provides a forum for chapter leaders to share insights, identify
regional needs and opportunities, and inform the development of initiatives that
support members, chapters, and the profession. Participation in the SAC helps ensure
that chapter perspectives are represented in regional discussions and strategic
2

planning efforts.
Chapter Presidents will receive an invitation when meetings for their respective
Regional SAC are scheduled and are encouraged to actively participate in these
discussions.
Governance
As an independent legal entity, the chapter is solely responsible for its own legal,
financial, and operational affairs. As Chapter President, you play a key role in
helping ensure the chapter operates in accordance with applicable laws and
regulations, the ISACA Chapter Affiliation Agreement, chapter bylaws and other
ISACA Global policies and requirements.
To support effective governance, the Chapter President should:
• Promote compliance with applicable laws, regulations, chapter governing
documents, and ISACA requirements.
• Help safeguard member and chapter data by supporting compliance with data
privacy and security requirements, including applicable local regulations (such as

GDPR) and ISACA policies.
•
• Lead the development and periodic review of the chapter's strategic plan in
collaboration with the board, and monitor progress toward established goals and
objectives.
• Implement the policies and decisions of the chapter board and support
accountability for their execution.
• Exercise appropriate executive leadership and judgment on operational matters
when specific policies or procedures do not exist, while remaining accountable to
the chapter board.
• Recommend the establishment of committees and, with board approval and in
accordance with the chapter bylaws, appoint committee chairs and other volunteer
leaders as needed.
• Serve as an ex officio member of all committees, except the Nominating Committee,
unless otherwise provided in the chapter bylaws.
• Oversee the nomination and election processes to help ensure compliance with the

chapter bylaws and applicable governance requirements.
• Work with the board and volunteer leaders to identify risks to achieving strategic
objectives and implement appropriate corrective actions when necessary.
• Ensure the chapter offers a sustainable portfolio of programs, events, and services
that provide value to members and support member engagement, professional
development, and chapter growth.
3

General Leadership
While the Chapter President provides leadership and oversight, responsibility for
governance and strategic direction rests with the chapter board collectively. The
President should work collaboratively with the board, committees, volunteers,
and staff to advance the chapter's mission and long-term sustainability.
The Chapter President should:
• Provide leadership in developing and maintaining an effective chapter governance
structure, including board and committee roles, responsibilities, and reporting
relationships, in accordance with the chapter bylaws.
• Foster clear communication, accountability, and collaboration among board
members, committee leaders, and volunteers.
• Inspire, support, recognize, and encourage board members, committee leaders,
and volunteers to advance the chapter's mission and strategic objectives.

• Promote a culture of teamwork, inclusion, professionalism, and volunteer
engagement throughout the chapter.
• Mentor and support officers, directors, committee chairs, and emerging leaders to
strengthen leadership development and succession planning.
• Lead and facilitate the chapter's annual strategic planning process, working with the
board to establish goals, objectives, priorities, and measures of success.
• Work with the board and volunteer leaders to establish an annual operating
calendar that supports timely execution of key chapter activities, governance
requirements, and strategic initiatives.
• Oversee periodic reviews of the chapter bylaws and governing documents and
recommend updates, as appropriate, to ensure continued relevance and
compliance.
• Provide oversight of chapter programs, events, communications, and marketing

activities to help ensure alignment with the chapter's strategic goals, brand
standards, and member needs.
• Provide oversight of the chapter's digital presence, including the chapter website
and social media channels, to help ensure content is accurate, current, and
consistent with ISACA and chapter policies.
• Supervise and support chapter staff, if any, in accordance with applicable
employment policies and board direction.
• Lead succession planning efforts for chapter leadership positions by identifying,
developing, and encouraging future leaders and volunteers in collaboration with the
board and committee leaders.
• Serve as the chapter's primary ambassador and relationship builder, fostering
collaboration with other professional organizations, community stakeholders,
ISACA chapters, and regional leaders where appropriate.

• Support membership growth, retention, and engagement efforts by working with the
Membership Director and other volunteers to develop and implement initiatives that
deliver value to members and recognize member contributions and achievements.
4

Finances
The Chapter President shares responsibility with the chapter board for fiduciary
oversight of the chapter and should work closely with the Chapter Treasurer to
promote sound financial management, transparency, and compliance. While
the Treasurer typically oversees the day-to-day administration of financial
activities, the President helps ensure appropriate financial controls, reporting,
and governance practices are in place.
The Chapter President should:
• Work with the Chapter Treasurer and board to help ensure compliance with
applicable financial, labor, tax, and regulatory requirements.
• Promote effective risk management and strong internal controls over chapter
finances.
o It is strongly recommended that chapters require dual authorization or
multiple signatures for disbursements exceeding a board-established

threshold and periodically review authorized signatories on all financial
accounts.
o It is strongly recommended that the Chapter President and/or Treasurer
regularly consult with the chapter's financial institution and financial
advisors, as appropriate, to assess and implement fraud prevention and risk
mitigation measures.
• Provide oversight of the chapter's budgeting, financial reporting, and financial
management processes to help ensure compliance with chapter policies,
applicable requirements, and generally accepted financial management practices.
• Review periodic financial reports and bank reconciliations with the Treasurer and
ensure that material discrepancies, unusual transactions, or control concerns are
promptly investigated and addressed.
• Help ensure that adequate financial records and supporting documentation are

maintained in accordance with the chapter's record retention policies and
applicable legal and regulatory requirements.
• Support the implementation and periodic review of a records retention policy. (An
example Record Retention Policy is included in the appendix of the Chapter
Treasurer Guidebook.)
• Ensure the board receives regular financial reports that accurately present chapter
revenues, expenses, assets, liabilities, and budget performance using the chapter's
established accounting structure.
• Encourage timely financial reporting and board review. Delays in producing financial
information may indicate operational or control issues and can limit the board's
ability to monitor financial performance, manage reserves, and take corrective
action when necessary.
• Work with the Treasurer and board to address identified financial risks, budget

variances, reserve shortfalls, or control deficiencies in a timely manner.
5

Effective financial stewardship is a shared responsibility of the chapter board. The President
should work collaboratively with the Treasurer and other board members to promote
accountability, transparency, and the long-term financial sustainability of the chapter.
Reporting
The Chapter President serves as the primary liaison between the chapter and ISACA
Global and helps ensure timely, accurate, and transparent reporting to both ISACA and
chapter stakeholders.
The Chapter President should:
• Serve as the primary point of contact with ISACA Global for the submission of
required chapter information, board rosters, reports, inquiries, and other official
communications.
• Work with the chapter board and applicable officers to ensure compliance with all
annual reporting requirements and deadlines established by ISACA.

o This includes ensuring chapter events are entered into the Engage platform,
required annual checklists are completed, and audit reports or financial
verification letters are submitted within required timeframes following the
chapter's Annual General Meeting (AGM).
o Coordinate the assignment, preparation, review, approval, and submission of
required reports and supporting documentation to ISACA Global.
• Establish and support effective reporting processes that provide the board with
timely information regarding chapter operations, strategic initiatives, membership
trends, program performance, and financial health.
• Ensure the board receives regular reports necessary to fulfill its governance,
oversight, and fiduciary responsibilities.
• Promote transparent communication with chapter members by providing regular

updates on chapter activities, achievements, strategic priorities, and financial
condition, as appropriate.
• Work with chapter officers, committee leaders, and volunteers to ensure reporting is
accurate, complete, and submitted in a timely manner.
• Promptly communicate significant chapter issues, risks, compliance concerns, or
operational challenges to the chapter board and ISACA Global, as appropriate.
Effective reporting supports transparency, accountability, informed decision-making,
and the chapter's ongoing compliance with both ISACA requirements and sound
association governance practices.
Meetings
The Chapter President is responsible for providing leadership during board and
membership meetings and helping ensure meetings are effective, productive,
and aligned with the chapter's strategic objectives. The President should

preside over chapter and board meetings whenever possible. If the President is
unable to attend, the Vice President or other designated officer should serve in
that capacity in accordance with the chapter bylaws.
6

The Chapter President should:
• Work with the Chapter Secretary and other appropriate officers to develop
agendas for board and membership meetings that focus on strategic
priorities, governance responsibilities, and key operational matters.
• Collaborate with the Chapter Treasurer to review proposed budgets, financial
reports, and significant financial matters before presentation to the board.
• Preside over regular and special meetings of the chapter and its board in
accordance with the chapter bylaws and applicable governance
requirements.
• Facilitate constructive discussion, encourage participation, and promote
informed decision-making by the board.
• Help ensure meeting agendas, materials, and supporting information are
distributed in advance to enable effective board deliberation and oversight.
• Maintain order during meetings and help ensure board business is conducted

fairly, efficiently, and in accordance with the chapter's governing documents
and adopted parliamentary procedures, if applicable.
• Ensure decisions, action items, and follow-up responsibilities are clearly
identified and appropriately documented.
• Encourage active engagement by directors, officers, committee chairs, and
other participants to support effective governance and leadership.
• Effective meetings enable the board to fulfill its governance responsibilities,
make informed decisions, and advance the chapter's mission, strategic goals,
and long-term sustainability.
Chapter Board Meetings
As required by the chapter bylaws, the chapter board should meet regularly
throughout the year, with a minimum of four board meetings annually. The
Chapter President should typically chair these meetings and help ensure they
are conducted effectively and in accordance with the chapter's governing

documents.
The Chapter President should be responsible for:
• Ensuring board meetings are conducted in compliance with the chapter bylaws,
applicable policies, and established governance practices.
• Presiding over board meetings and facilitating productive discussion, informed
decision-making, and appropriate board oversight.
• Recognizing, presenting, and ruling on motions in accordance with the chapter's
adopted meeting procedures and parliamentary authority, if applicable.
• Helping ensure that all directors have an opportunity to participate in discussions
and deliberations.
• Maintaining order and ensuring meetings are conducted efficiently and
professionally.
• Confirming that board decisions, motions, and action items are clearly documented
by the Secretary.
• Working with the board and Secretary to establish the date, time, and format of

future meetings and communicate meeting schedules to board members in a timely
manner.
• Monitoring follow-up actions arising from board meetings and supporting
accountability for the completion of assigned tasks.
• Effective board meetings are essential to fulfilling the board's governance
7

responsibilities, overseeing chapter operations, and advancing the chapter's
strategic objectives.
Regular or Special Membership Meetings
As required by the chapter bylaws, the chapter should hold membership meetings as
specified in its governing documents. The Chapter President should typically preside over
these meetings and help ensure they are conducted in a manner that promotes
transparency, member engagement, and effective governance.
The Chapter President should:
• Ensure membership meetings are conducted in accordance with the chapter
bylaws, applicable policies, and established governance practices.
• Preside over regular, annual, and special membership meetings, as applicable.
• Facilitate orderly and productive discussions while encouraging member
participation and engagement.
• Recognize, present, and rule on motions in accordance with the chapter's adopted

meeting procedures and parliamentary authority, if applicable.
• Maintain order and ensure business is conducted fairly, professionally, and
efficiently.
• Ensure members are provided with appropriate information regarding chapter
activities, strategic priorities, governance matters, and financial performance, as
appropriate.
• Work with the Chapter Secretary to ensure meeting proceedings, decisions, and
actions are accurately documented.
• Coordinate with the board and chapter leadership to schedule and communicate
membership meetings in accordance with bylaw requirements and notice
provisions.
The Chapter President's responsibilities for membership meetings are generally
consistent with those described under Chapter Board Meetings, with an additional
emphasis on member communication, engagement, and transparency. Membership

meetings provide an important opportunity to inform members, gather feedback, and
strengthen the connection between the chapter's leadership and its membership.
Immediately Following the Annual General Meeting
Leadership Transition and Reporting
Following the chapter's Annual General Meeting (AGM), or whenever a change in
leadership
occurs, the outgoing Chapter President should promptly notify the Chapter
Experience team through ISACA Support of all newly elected and appointed
chapter leaders. This helps ensure chapter records remain accurate and that
new leaders receive timely access to chapter resources, communications,
systems, and support.
8

passages.section: The outgoing Chapter President should also:
passages.text:
The outgoing Chapter President should also:
• Ensure that chapter officer and board member information is updated in
accordance with ISACA requirements.
• Facilitate a timely and effective leadership transition by transferring relevant
records, documentation, credentials, and institutional knowledge to
incoming leaders.
• Work with incoming officers to ensure continuity of chapter operations,
governance activities, and strategic initiatives.
• Confirm that banking, financial, legal, and administrative records are
updated as necessary to reflect leadership changes.
• Support the onboarding of new leaders and encourage their participation in
available ISACA training, resources, and leadership development
opportunities.
9

passages.section: Chapter Leader Listing on Hosted Chapter Websites
passages.text:
Chapter Leader Listing on Hosted Chapter Websites
Chapter site administrators are responsible for managing the content displayed
on the chapter's About Us page within chapter websites hosted on ISACA
Engage. Each chapter may determine the approach that best fits its needs,
while considering member privacy, ease of maintenance, and the desired level
of visibility for chapter leaders.
Options for displaying chapter leadership information include:
• Manually maintain leadership information by entering and updating board and
committee leader details as changes occur. This option provides the greatest
flexibility and control over content, format, and display. Example: Milwaukee
Chapter.
• Display limited information and provide a general chapter contact method rather
than listing individual leaders. This approach may be preferred by chapters seeking

Mentoring
The Chapter President and Vice President should actively support the
development, engagement, and success of chapter volunteers. Providing
guidance, coaching, and leadership development opportunities helps
strengthen volunteer effectiveness, build future leaders, and support the long-
term sustainability of the chapter.
10

The Chapter President should:
• Encourage and support the professional growth and development of
chapter volunteers, committee members, and emerging leaders.
• Work with the Vice President, board members, and committee chairs to
provide orientation, mentoring, coaching, and ongoing support to
volunteers, as appropriate.
• Monitor volunteer engagement and performance and provide constructive
feedback when expectations, responsibilities, or commitments are not
being met.
• Address performance concerns in a timely and professional manner
through coaching, mentoring, role clarification, or other appropriate
support measures.
• Collaborate with board members and committee leaders to identify and
develop future chapter leaders and promote leadership succession
planning.
• Foster a positive volunteer experience that encourages continued
engagement, leadership development, and knowledge transfer.

Succession Planning
Chapters are encouraged to establish leadership development and succession
planning practices that help ensure continuity of operations and governance.
One approach is to create a President-Elect, Deputy Director, or similar
leadership development position that allows an emerging leader to gain
experience and prepare for future service as Chapter President.
Such positions can provide:
• A structured transition and leadership development period for future
chapter leaders.
• Opportunities for mentoring and knowledge transfer from current leaders.
• Greater leadership continuity and organizational resilience.
• Enhanced volunteer engagement and leadership pipeline development.
If a chapter chooses to establish a President-Elect, Deputy Director, or similar
position, the role, responsibilities, authority, and succession provisions should

be clearly defined in the chapter's bylaws.
11

Turnover Procedures
Leadership Transition and Handover
A well-planned leadership transition helps maintain operational continuity, preserve
institutional knowledge, and position the chapter for future success. The outgoing
Chapter President should work closely with incoming leaders, officers,
directors, committee chairs, and volunteers to ensure a timely and effective transfer of
responsibilities.
As part of the leadership transition process, the outgoing Chapter President
should:
• Ensure the timely transfer of relevant chapter records, files, correspondence,
credentials, and institutional knowledge to incoming officers, directors,
committee chairs, and other authorized leaders.
• Confirm that all required annual reporting and compliance obligations have been
completed or appropriately assigned, including any reports due to ISACA Global.

• Establish a transition timeline and target completion date for all turnover
activities.
• Coordinate with chapter officers, directors, and committee chairs to review and
update chapter procedures, forms, operational documentation, and governance
records, as appropriate.
• Prepare, or coordinate the preparation of, a list of open items and ongoing
activities requiring follow-up by incoming leaders. Examples may include:
o Outstanding invoices awaiting payment approval or processing.
o Venue, facility, or service contracts for upcoming chapter events.
o Speaker, instructor, sponsor, or vendor agreements for future programs.
o Strategic initiatives, projects, or operational matters that remain
incomplete.
o Other commitments, obligations, or action items requiring continued
attention.
• Facilitate transition meetings between outgoing and incoming leaders to support

knowledge transfer, answer questions, and promote continuity. These meetings
may be conducted individually or as a group, depending on the chapter's needs.
• Work with the Treasurer to review and update the chapter's inventory of assets,
equipment, records, and other chapter property.
• Ensure that all chapter-owned property, records, and resources are appropriately
transferred to authorized incoming leaders.
• Confirm that banking, financial, and other administrative accounts are updated as
necessary to reflect leadership changes, including authorized signatories.
Chapters are encouraged to maintain multiple authorized signers and appropriate
internal controls in accordance with board-approved policies.
• Ensure access to chapter mailboxes, post office boxes, technology platforms,
websites, social media accounts, cloud storage, email systems, and other chapter

resources is transferred to authorized incoming leaders and removed for outgoing
leaders, as appropriate.
• Transfer current correspondence files and other important records to the
incoming Chapter President, including materials, resources, and guidance
12

provided by ISACA Global that may support future chapter operations.
Recognition and Appreciation
The outgoing Chapter President should also consider coordinating a volunteer
Recognition activity or event to acknowledge and celebrate the contributions of board
members, committee leaders, volunteers, and members whose efforts supported the
chapter's success throughout the year.
Appendix
Timetable for Action
President’s Annual Checklist
• Ensure all chapter events are included on the Engage chapter website.
• Between 1 November – 31 December each year,
o Submit the online compliance checklist.
o Submit the audit or financial verification letter to ISACA Global.
o Submit any other mandatory items to ISACA Global as needed.
o Conduct an orientation for all incoming chapter leaders. Include:
 Mission and vision statements
 Organizational history
 Bylaws and policies
 Strategic plan

 Financial summaries
 Committee information
 Meeting processes
 Chapter Affiliation Agreement
o Submit the list of volunteers appointed and elected at the AGM to
the Chapter Experience team via ISACA Support.
13

o Develop chapter goals and strategies for the new year via a strategic
planning session.
o Ensure all volunteers have signed and submitted to the chapter’s secretary the
Conflict of Interest Statement and the Willingness to Serve Agreement.
• Within 60 days of the AGM:
o Ensure the chapter’s goals and strategic plans are in progress.
• Within 210 days (approximately 7 months) of the AGM:
o Begin recruiting volunteers for the following year/term.
